question.problem: Given that the random variable $Y∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{5}),$ calculate $P(Y\le 4).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $Y$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda y}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
Y∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{5}).
$$

So, $Y$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{e}^{-2y/5}, & y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(Y\le 4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 4) & ={\int }_{0}^{4}f(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{2}{5}{e}^{-2y/5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{e}^{-2y/5}{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =-{e}^{-8/5}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.7981\end{aligned}
$$
